text:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT CREATED • kv-cache-explosion detected in paged-block-manager on us-east-1 hosts (severity: P1) :rotating_light:

Alex Chen: seeing continuous batch size ramp at ~02:24 UTC, mem resident rising across the pool, OOM-ish evictions starting 02:28. dashboards -> https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/kv-cache

Maya Patel: confirmed, 95p latency spiking from 120ms -> 2.1s on generation routes. token throughput dropped ~35%. :eyes:

Jordan (oncall): taking lead. Jordan -> Alex/Maya: can you drop a quick summary of which services impacted and any obvious config delta?

Alex Chen: root cause suspicion: recent batch-config roll (auto-batch window increased from 10ms -> 40ms) + new block-size heuristic landed in block-manager last deploy. Combined they created long-lived big KV blocks and metadata growth.

Samir Garg: logs show repeated "block-meta-growth" warnings. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:26:12Z] WARN block-manager: block-meta-size=124MB, block-count=978
[2026-03-15T02:26:12Z] WARN kv-cache: continuous-batch.size=384, prefix-hit=0.03
```

Maya Patel: customer impact: three mid-market customers saw generation failures (429/503) between 02:30-02:40. CS-Leads fyi, might get escalations.

CS-Leads: we're pinging affected accounts, prepping statement. we need ETA for mitigation.

Jordan (oncall): mitigation plan, immediate -> throttle continuous batching to conservative defaults, enable aggressive eviction, and revert block-size heuristic if safe; hotpatch if needed. Can infra apply throttles?

InfraBot: Patch plan: 1) update feature flag `continuous_batch_window_ms` to 10ms for pool-prod-us-east-1 2) set `block_manager.eviction_policy=aggressive` 3) enable prefix-kv-trimming=true. Ops commands prepared.

Alex Chen: verified config rollback command:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/kv-serving continuous_batch_window_ms=10 --record
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/block-manager block_manager.eviction_policy=aggressive --record
```

Samir Garg: I'll apply the env changes to 3 nodes first as canary, watch for drop in memory and latency.

Jordan (oncall): please do canary now, post metrics 1/5/15m after. If stable, rollout full. Keep notes for postmortem.

Alex Chen: canary applied to kv-serving-2/3/4 at 02:33. initial memory delta: -18% on canary pods after 60s.

Maya Patel: latency 95p on canary fell from 1.9s -> 210ms within 90s. token throughput recovered gradually. :thumbsup:

Samir Garg: rolling to remaining nodes at 02:36, using 30s stagger. watching block-manager metrics; block-meta-size trending down.

Jordan (oncall): CS-Leads, please stand by for customer update: we expect mitigation effective by 02:38, full recovery by 02:45 pending no regressions.

CS-Leads: message queued to customers: "We've applied throttles and mitigations; service should recover in minutes. We'll follow up with root-cause analysis."

Alex Chen: note: we found a metadata leak in block-manager where abandoned block refs weren't being freed if batch size > 256 and prefix-hit < 0.05. Created hotfix PR #4782 to fix deref path.

Samir Garg: PR looks safe, running quick unit + e2e on staging. plan to deploy hotfix after full rollout of throttles to prevent re-trigger.

Jordan (oncall): timeline: canary success -> full throttle rollout complete 02:38 -> hotfix PR merge + deploy 02:48 -> monitor 1hr. If any regressions, rollback throttle and escalate to infra-leads.

InfraBot: Full rollout applied at 02:38. Verified: mem aggregate down 22%, 95p latency normalized to ~140ms, no further 5xx spikes in next 5m.

Maya Patel: customers reporting service normal for the three impacted tenants. CS-Leads continuing outbound.

Alex Chen: merged PR #4782 at 02:47, deployed to canary group 02:50. No anomalies on canary after 10m. planning full deploy 03:05.

Jordan (oncall): handing off to next oncall for long-window monitoring. @Samir you're SC for postmortem — capture timeline, cluster configs, and diff of the batch heuristic change.

Samir Garg: ack. I'll draft postmortem and put remediation items: 1) stricter gating of batch-config increases with load tests 2) add OOM-like metadata leak alarm 3) rollback-safe feature flagging for block-manager heuristics.

IncidentBot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 03:10 after sustained stabilization.

Jordan (oncall): official handoff to @Lina (next oncall) at 03:12. Lina please monitor for 4 hours and escalate if any reappearance.

Samir Garg: will attach logs/graphs to the postmortem and schedule a small AS/QA run to validate batch window changes.

CS-Leads: closing customer comms after final confirmation, will post summary to the affected accounts.

Alex Chen: final note — we might want to add a short-circuit that forces prefix-KV trimming when block-meta-size > 80MB to avoid future blowups. Adding to backlog. :memo:
